Why a corpus was withdrawn, and when.

An export is immutable and a withdrawal does not change that: the manifest
keeps every count, digest and exclusion it had. What is gone is the rows,
because the alternative is a published corpus holding words somebody asked
to have deleted — and an erasure that stopped at the archive would be an
erasure in name only.

conversations.description: The conversations whose erasure caused this.

WorkAssignment.description: One attempt, and everything performing it needs.

context_id.description:
`<execution>/<step>/<attempt>` — what the work is idempotent by, and
what a task with a side effect keys it on.

inputs.description:
What the parents produced, by name. The bytes are read one at a time
through this attempt's own `inputs/{name}` route.

is_retake.description:
Whether somebody else held this attempt first.

The reactor asks its runtime by idempotency key before re-running a
takeover, because a timeout proves nothing about whether the previous
call finished. A worker has no such lookup to offer, so it is told
instead: a task with a side effect must be idempotent by `context_id`,
and this is when that matters.

lease_expires_at.description:
When this claim stops being trusted unless it is renewed.

An instant rather than a duration, and the difference matters: a worker
told "five minutes" has to agree with this process about when the five
minutes started, and the two clocks are the whole question. A deadline
is one fact. It also means a client cannot hard-code the lease length
and keep beating at the wrong rate the day the rule moves —
`aiwatcher_jobs` owns that number, and nothing here restates it.

outputs.description: Named row outputs required by the pinned plan.

parameters.description: What the run itself was started with.

report_idempotent.description: The result route can acknowledge a matching outcome from durable history.

task_ref.description:
`name@version`, from the plan. The worker matches it against what it
registered; the server already did, which is why this is a fact rather
than a request.

timeout_seconds.description: The step's own deadline. Past it the server stops waiting for a report.

workflow_id.description: Correlation supplied by the platform; the worker emits only child spans.

oneOf.description: It ran and produced something.

cacheable.description:
Whether this may answer for its cache key later. The worker
answers it because only the process that ran the work knows what it
managed to do.

outputs.description: References this attempt's own `outputs/{name}` route handed back.

result.description:
A bounded control value. Rows go in an artifact — a result that
grows with the data is one that eventually cannot be replayed.

oneOf.description: It did not.

class.description:
Whether trying again could plausibly produce a different answer.
The worker classifies it, because the process that made the call is
the one that knows.

WorkReport.description: What a worker did with its attempt.

WorkerBody.description: A worker saying which attempt it is talking about.

WorkerReport.description:
A report, with the worker that is making it.

Two structs rather than a flattened one: serde's `flatten` and
`deny_unknown_fields` do not compose, and the report is a tagged enum whose
variants are the whole point of the body being checked.

payloads.description:
Where this run's words live. Recorded rather than looked up, so an
append can be checked against what the run was started under years
after the deployment's default moved.

oneOf.description:
Take a failed or crashed step again, from its pinned inputs and code.
Historical attempts are preserved; this is a new one.
The answer a `HumanInput` step asked for.

Dispatch one attempt. The effect command a reactor deduplicates by
`command_id`, and the row a worker claims.

idempotency_key.description:
The stable idempotency key: `<execution>/<step>/<attempt>`. What a
reactor asks a runtime by before it retries a timeout.

oneOf.description:
Put a question in front of somebody. Not dispatched to anything: the
answer arrives as `ProvideInput`.

WorkflowCommand.description:
What somebody wants to happen.

Two families in one enum, and the split is by who sends it. The first six
are **intentions** the API accepts from a caller. `ExecuteStep` and
`RequestInput` are **effects** the decider emits for a reactor or a worker
to pick up; they never reach the event log, because ADR_0026 keeps the
reasoning in the store and puts only facts about work on the log.

WorkflowDefinition.description: A workflow as the catalog holds it.

version.description:
Content hash of the declared topology, chosen by the producer.

Not interpreted here beyond equality: a changed version replaces the
stored shape. It exists so re-declaring on every execution — which is
what keeps the catalog alive across retention eviction — costs nothing
when the shape has not moved.

WorkflowEdge.description: One declared edge. Direction is `from → to`.

oneOf.description:
The delay before a retry may be dispatched, resolved to an instant here
so that replay reaches the same schedule.

result.description: A bounded control value. Rows go in an artifact.

oneOf.description:
The step was answered from an earlier identical one, and this records
which artifacts were reused. A hit is an execution state, not a silence.

It names the **attempt** it answered, because that attempt was claimed
and dispatched like any other: something has to settle its row, or it
stays claimable behind a lease nobody releases.
The step will not run: something it needed did not succeed.

A cancel was accepted. Cooperative: running steps are asked to stop, and
`ExecutionCancelled` follows when they have.

WorkflowEvent.description:
What happened.

The ones a reactor or a worker reports — `StepStarted`, `StepCompleted`,
`StepFailed` — arrive as *inputs* to the decider, because the decider did
not know them: something outside performed the effect and came back. Every
other variant is an output the decider produced.

allOf.description:
A hosted decider's message. Neither a command this engine may refuse nor
an event it folds: [`Self::event`] and [`Self::command`] both answer
`None`, so `decide`'s replay skips it by construction rather than by
somebody remembering to.

oneOf.description:
A hosted decider's message. Neither a command this engine may refuse nor
an event it folds: [`Self::event`] and [`Self::command`] both answer
`None`, so `decide`'s replay skips it by construction rather than by
somebody remembering to.

WorkflowMessage.description: One thing in the stream, whichever kind it is.

WorkflowNode.description: One node of a declared graph.

agent.description: The agent expected to run it, when the graph names one.

kind.description:
What kind of work it is — `chain`, `retriever`, `agent`, whatever the
producer calls it. Free text on purpose: the same reason
`data.step_type` is free text, so a new kind is not a backend release.

WorkflowSpec.description: A workflow's executable definition, saved by content before it is run.

version.description: The application's release label; the immutable identity is the revision digest.

WorkflowTask.description:
One step of a workflow: work a worker runs, or a gate that waits.

Two shapes in one struct rather than a tagged union, because a definition is
content-addressed and stored: every revision saved before gates existed has
to keep parsing and keep hashing to the same revision. An internally tagged
enum has no default tag, so it would have refused all of them. `approval`
is what decides which shape this is, and the fields the other shape needs
are refused by name when it is set.

oneOf.description: Set to make this step a gate: it waits for a person and runs nothing.

outputs.description: Named row artifacts this step produces.

task_ref.description:
A registered function's name and pinned version. Never an import path to
execute. Empty on a gate, which runs nothing.

timeout_seconds.description:
How long an attempt may take. Absent on a gate: nothing dispatches a
wait, so no timer is ever armed and a number here would be a deadline
the code does not keep.
